title: Chapter 107: Invisible Customer
html:
Chen Ge placed the doll his parents had left him and Doctor Skull-cracker’s hammer beside the bed. Everything is ready.

He switched off the light, plugged in his phone, and left it recording on the bedside table. Then he crawled beneath the bed with the fearsome hammer. Candlelight flickered across the room. The moment he closed his eyes, terrifying possibilities crowded his mind.

Curled on his side with his head near the bed frame, he remained alert to every sound. Through the half-open door, he could see the slippers in the corridor.

The slippers are where they were, and the white rice has remained unmoved. I wonder why the black phone asked me to prepare these things.

The candle shortened as his eyelids grew heavy. Night settled over the Haunted House. Exhausted by days without proper rest, Chen Ge resisted a little longer before sleep claimed him.

…

Cold touched his calf. Chen Ge opened his eyes. The candle was out, and the room lay silent in darkness.

What time is it?Chen Ge wanted to glance at his watch, but he realized he could not move.

Sleep paralysis?

He did not waste strength struggling. Sleep paralysis did not prevent him from breathing, so he steadied each breath and concentrated on bending one finger. He kept his gaze fixed there. If something terrifying was nearby, seeing it while unable to move would only feed his panic.

After three minutes, his little finger twitched. It was a beginning. As he concentrated on the next, his gaze passed the open door and a question surfaced. When I set down the slippers, were their toes pointing in or out?

He had positioned them for someone leaving the room, so they should have faced outward. Now their toes pointed into the bedroom.

Did I misplace them earlier?

Dread tightened his stomach as he fought to move his other fingers. The candle had long since died. Something shuffled through the room, disturbing the rice scattered across the floor.

As he watched, one slipper lurched forward with the awkwardness of someone learning to walk.

It moved!

The more anxious he became, the less his body responded. After that first halting step, both slippers advanced several paces as though worn by invisible feet.

The invisible customer is already here? Why can’t I see him?

While he watched, the slippers reached the control-room door and stopped. The door swung open by itself, then closed again. Every window in the Haunted House was shut; no wind had moved it.

What is it looking for?

The slippers wandered the dark corridor before stopping at the dressing room. From beneath the bed, Chen Ge could see that the mirror’s black covering had been removed. The mask stitched from many faces swayed before the glass.

Alarmed, he fought harder to move. At that moment, the swaying mask went still. The hollows behind its eyes seemed to stare directly at his hiding place.

I’ve been discovered!

The mask dropped to the floor, and the dressing-room door slammed shut. The slippers paused outside, turned toward Chen Ge, and hurried to the staff break room.

Trapped beneath the bed, Chen Ge could only watch them approach. The break-room door opened wider, and the slippers stopped beside him.

He closed his eyes and feigned sleep. Cold air brushed his face, and faint breathing stirred beside his ear, as though someone had leaned close to inspect him.

It’s checking whether I’m truly asleep.He dared not look. Whatever he saw might shatter his composure.

Unable to move, pretending to sleep was his only defense. Several seconds later, the icy breathing ceased. He opened his eyes a fraction. Nothing stood before him. The slippers remained beside the bed, but their toes now faced the corridor.

Did it climb into my bed?The thought made him shiver. This thing might have roamed the Haunted House every night while he slept. If it meant him harm, the consequences were unthinkable.

The slippers remained still. Whatever wore them was probably lying above him. This was his chance. He poured every ounce of concentration into the one finger he could move, fighting to release the rest of his body. Completing the Nightmare Mission no longer mattered. Helplessness inside his own flesh was unbearable.

The black phone’s missions had hardened his concentration. Gradually, his other fingers responded. He closed them into a fist, and sensation crept back into his arm.

A little more. Just a little more.The muscles in his arm strained. His breathing steadied, and he managed to turn his neck. If his legs awakened, he would regain full control—and with the hammer in hand, he would no longer be defenseless.

His lower body remained numb. Heartbeat pounding in his ears, he forced himself onto his side. The instant he turned toward the wall, the invisible shackles broke.

Control returned all at once. Then he looked behind him, and gooseflesh swept across his skin.

There was a girl lying behind him.

The monster didn’t get onto the bed! It has been behind me all along!

His hand shot toward the hammer. The girl behind him realized that he had broken free of the paralysis.

She reacted a beat too slowly. Their eyes met; then she dissolved into shadow and fled the room.

Chen Ge grabbed the hammer and chased after her.

The girl’s face had looked strangely familiar.
